title: Peameal, Egg & Cheddar Breakfast Sandwiches
subtitle: better-than-the-drive-thru English muffins with Toronto's own peameal bacon
imageAlt: Two toasted English muffin breakfast sandwiches with peameal bacon, a round egg and melted cheddar on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 4 sandwiches: 2 each, or 1 each plus 2 for the freezer

beforeYouStart.text: A clean wide-mouth canning ring (or a crumpled foil ring) makes the egg perfectly round.
Split the muffins with a fork for the craggiest toast.

steps.title: Peameal
steps.text: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium. Cook the peameal 3–4 minutes a side, until golden and 71°C (160°F). Set aside on a plate.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast the English muffins and spread with half the butter.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Melt the rest of the butter in the skillet over medium-low. Set greased rings in the pan, crack an egg into each and break the yolk with a fork. Season, add 2 tbsp water to the pan, cover and cook 3–4 minutes, until fully set.

steps.title: Stack
steps.text: Lift off the rings, top each egg with cheddar and cover 30 seconds to melt. Stack muffin, peameal, cheesy egg, muffin.

fixIt.fix: Grease the inside of the ring well with butter or oil.
Cook just to 71°C (160°F); it's lean and dries out quickly.
Toast until really golden and assemble right before eating.

saleTip: Buy a whole peameal roast on sale and slice it yourself; it's cheaper per kilo than pre-sliced.
swap: Back bacon or deli ham for peameal. Fried egg folded in quarters if you don't have rings.
leftovers: Wrap cooled sandwiches in parchment and foil and freeze.
doneness: Peameal bacon (pork) to 71°C (160°F); eggs cooked until firm (Health Canada). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on classic Canadian peameal bacon and tested homemade English muffin sandwich methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): ring-set steamed eggs and pan-seared peameal.
prepAhead: Make a batch and freeze up to 1 month for grab-and-go mornings.
reheat: From frozen: unwrap, wrap in a paper towel and microwave 1½–2 minutes, flipping once, until 74°C (165°F).
airFryer: Cook the peameal slices at 190°C (375°F) for 6–8 minutes, flipping halfway, to 71°C (160°F), and toast the muffins in the basket for 2–3 minutes. Reheat frozen sandwiches (unwrapped) at 160°C (325°F) for 10–12 minutes until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Egg and cheddar sandwiches; no peameal.

fancy.note: A crispy hash brown patty and a swipe of maple mayo inside each one.

addSteps.title: Hash browns
addSteps.text: Start first: bake the hash brown patties at 220°C (425°F) for 15–18 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp (or air-fry 10 minutes at 200°C / 400°F). Stir the mayo and maple syrup, spread on the muffin tops and tuck a patty into each sandwich.

plating: Wrap the bottom half in parchment, diner-style.
Cut one in half to show the layers.

why.0-1: Peameal is lean cured pork loin rolled in cornmeal: Toronto's signature bacon.
why.0-3: Breaking the yolk and steaming under a lid sets the egg evenly and keeps it from dripping.

funFact: Peameal bacon was first rolled in ground dried peas; the switch to cornmeal came after the First World War.

keeps.note: wrap each sandwich in parchment then foil
keeps.thaw: No need to thaw: reheat from frozen until 74°C (165°F) in the centre

drink: Coffee, double-double if you like, or an orange juice.
